entries.title: Civic
entries.epigraph: _"If the [[Pillars]] of [[Civilization]] are what builds its tenets, [[Civic]] are what makes them real through practices, tradition, culture, and everyday life. A [[Civilization]] is the song it chooses to sing."_
entries.summary: These are the unit blocks that form the identity and [[Resonance]] of any [[Civilization]]. It encodes activities, laws, culture, rituals, and practices that codify and integrate the [[Arcanoria]]'s deep magical laws with the governance of its empires.
entries.body:
These are the unit blocks that form the identity and [[Resonance]] of any [[Civilization]]. It encodes activities, laws, culture, rituals, and practices that codify and integrate the [[Arcanoria]]'s deep magical laws with the governance of its empires. Thus [[Civic]]s are very versatile and evolve to reflect the progression of [[Humanity]] through the [[Ages]] and their evolving relationship with magic, crisis, and power.

[[Civic]] occupy too the spectrum of [[Consonance]] and [[Dissonance]], which can range between idyllic democratic practices to horrific military tactics. They are divided into the same categories as [[Enclave]]s:

- Agromagical [[Civic]]: Growth, Health, Sanitation, Sustenance.
- Militant [[Civic]]: Tactics, Weapons, Mercenaries, Hunters.
- Auric [[Civic]]: [[Aureus Pillar]], [[Piety]], [[Faith]], Knowledge, Science.
- Weaver [[Civic]]: [[Waltz Pillar]], Culture, Poetry, Songs, Communal Arts.
- Domestication [[Civic]]: Creatures, [[Pure Light]], Taming, Druids.
- Trading [[Civic]]: Economics, Wealth, [[Resources]], Efficiency.
- Industrious [[Civic]]: Equipment, Forges, Artisans, Metalworks.
- Regal [[Civic]]: [[Regalia Pillar]], Politics, Diplomacy, Prestige, Espionage.
- Indulgent [[Civic]]: Entertainment, Pleasure, Joy, Luxuries,
- Esoteric [[Civic]]: [[Chorus Pillar]], [[Outer God]]s, Dark [[Magic Arts]], Witchcraft, Spirits.

### Tier 1 [[Ages]] [[Civic]]s ([[Ages]] 0 - III)

### Agromagical, Indulgent, Weaver & Domestication [[Civic]]s

**Culinary Alchemists | Agromagical [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] I-III | [[Consonance]]**

Practical magical cooking using locally harvested ingredients to create temporary spell enhancements. All the recipes are shared communally, and each village maintains a Flavor Log recording which ingredient combinations produce stable [[Resonance]]. Chefs are considered essential laborers.

[[Ballad]]s:

- In a starving settlement, an untalented chef finds an ancient recipe capable of stabilizing the entire village's psychological [[Composure]]. Because the required rare ingredient is deep within a deadly [[Vibrational Fallout]] zone, the chef must convince a traumatized, half-broken [[Spellweaver]] to escort them, turning foraging into a desperate fight for survival.

**Feast of Abundance | Indulgent [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] I-III | [[Consonance]]**

Surplus goods and [[Auric Peach]]es are thrown from towers into public squares in a mandatory act of redistribution. Wealth held past the festival date is taxed as hoarding. [[Legend]]s in power who give the most during the feast earn higher social legitimacy, and some communities maintain records of each feast's yields and distribution, and farmers are honored as [[Civic]] [[Pillars]] equal to [[Spellweaver]]s.

[[Ballad]]s:

- A manipulative aristocrat attempts a bloodless coup by hiding vast wealth in magical [[Void]]-pockets to evade the hoarding tax, planning a massive distribution to instantly buy the public's loyalty. An undercover Justiciar must expose this economic sabotage before the feast crowns a tyrant.

**[[Ballad]] & Fantasy Plays | Weaver [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] II–IV | [[Consonance]]**

The formal organization of writers, singers, poets, and composers into state-sanctioned guilds designed to create culture, new stories, and preserve the [[Ballad]]s of [[Legend]]s. The classical civilization of [[Iridia]] is noted as a major patron of this [[Civic]], officially sponsoring writers of fiction and fairytales to weave them into the empire's culture.

[[Ballad]]s:

- A state-sponsored playwright uncovers a "[[Scorching Truth]]"— on how the [[Civilization]]'s founding hero was actually a cowardly deserter that became an [[Atonalis]]. Knowing the [[Auric Order]] executes those holding forbidden knowledge, the playwright encodes the truth into a propagandist play, sparking a psychological thriller of censorship and treason under the king's nose in a play akin to Shakespeare's Hamlet.

**Ritual [[Whistling Fans]] Dancers | Weaver [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] II–VI | [[Consonance]]**

Cultural and martial ceremonies inspired by [[Sephira]] (the [[Mythic Virtuoso]] of [[Cindergale]]), which utilize [[Whistling Fans]] as a formal patronage to the arts of [[Dance]] and martial combat.

[[Ballad]]s:

- During a grand martial ceremony, a young dancer realizes their rival's [[Whistling Fans]] are tuned to a [[Dissonance]] designed to shatter their internal [[Coherence]] and trigger a panic attack that interrupts the ceremony to crown them de jure heir. The dancer must instantly adapt their choreography to survive a deadly acoustic battle disguised as a synchronized duet.

**Moonlit Vigil | Weaver [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0-III | [[Consonance]]**

Courtship rituals in [[Glimmerfern]] groves during a full [[Moon]]. In silence people meet a matching frequency. Practiced by [[Waltz Pillar]], [[Chorus Pillar]], peasants and refugees. It is a _The folk tradition of the broken world._ in the last pockets that dim with hope to create love.

[[Ballad]]s:

- A noble [[Spellweaver]] sneaks into a peasant Vigil and falls deeply in love by phase-locking in perfect [[Sympathetic Vibration]] with a commoner [[Spellweaver]]. When their family demands a loveless political marriage, the couple must choose whether to sever their true magical connection or ignite a civil war.

**The Ball Fluff Runs | Domestication [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] I-VI | [[Consonance]]**

Periodic runs through city streets pursued by specially bred [[Pure Light]] creatures that are giant fluff sticky balls, whomever reaches the finish line without being touched by one gets to win the produce of these domesticated creatures.

**Horned Flag Stampedes | Domestication [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] II-VI | [[Cusp]]

Runs inspired by the Ball Fluff Runs but using bull-like [[Pure Light]] creatures which have [[Crystal]]-tipped horns. During these runs, regular people can get injured, and there are several flags left in the arena, the survivors who earn the most flags while still standing in the arena of the bulls gets to have a feast with the cooked [[Pure Light]] creatures afterward.

### Auric, Trading & Industrious [[Civic]]s

[[Demi-Human]] Slave Trade [[Dissonance]]

indentured Servitude [[Dissonance]]

### Regal, Militant & Esoteric [[Civic]]s

**Truth [[Soul Leitmotif]] Testimonies | Regal [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] I Onwards | [[Consonance]]

A legal and social practice that requires individuals to use the dormant state of their [[Soul Leitmotif]] when signing social contracts. Because the [[Soul Leitmotif]] is a physical crystallization of one's [[Consciousness]] and emotional truth, this [[Civic]] effectively uses the bare soul as a flawless lie detector to build social harmony and trust.

[[Ballad]]s:

- An infamous spy infiltrates a rival empire to sign a doomed peace treaty, using [[Illusory Magic]] to project a false aura of Pristine [[Composure]] over their corrupted soul while framing the legitimate ruler of lying by flickering conflict to their [[Soul Leitmotif]]. A low-ranking clerk spots a microscopic flicker of [[Dissonance]] and must prove the deception before war erupts.

**Harmonic Quorum | Regal [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] I-III | [[Consonance]]**

Major policy decisions require a [[Resonance]] as majority vote. The assembled leadership must attuned their internal [[Coherence]] and [[Soul Leitmotif]]s onto a single frequency. If the leaders cannot achieve [[Sympathetic Vibration]] due to doubt or conflict, the policy cannot pass.

[[Ballad]]s:

- The council has one hour to pass a defensive edict against an encroaching demon swarm, but the Quorum fails because one hidden member is secretly terrified and generating [[Discordant Interference]]. The protagonist must interrogate the council's minds to find the coward before the walls are breached.

**Bridal Conquest | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0–III | [[Cusp]]**

A political and martial practice involving the capture of enemy rulers or high-ranking knights of the opposite sex to marry them into their [[Civilization]]. This [[Civic]] provides a the Bridal casus belli. Allowing [[Civilization]] to capture opposing enemies and instead of executing them, the ritual of courtship is meant to systematically create and secure strong lineages of magical heirs that unify cultures.

[[Ballad]]s:

- An undefeated warlord is forced into marriage with the empress who decimated their homeland. Over years, they develop genuine love. Just as they admit their [[Resonance]], the warlord's former generals breach the capital to assassinate the empress, forcing the warlord to turn against their own people to protect their captor.

**Grand Hunts of [[Legend]]s | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] II–IV | [[Consonance]]**

Coordinated hunting parties of great renown of top [[Spellweaver]]s in groups of 4 to 7, each assigned a specific role, to track and kill high-ranking [[Atonalis]] and [[Pure Light]] Behemoths. Successful hunts forge permanent synergy bonds, prestige, and yield pristine rare materials, pelts, and [[Rose Seed]]s.

[[Ballad]]s:

- Tracking an [[Ascendant]] [[Atonalis]] into a collapsed pass, a hunting party realizes the monster is perfectly anticipating them because it is the shattered [[Soul Leitmotif]] of their original mentor. Their fallen mentor uses the shared memories to turn the hunters against one another, and exploit their individual weaknesses.

**Duels of Severance | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0-III | [[Cusp]]**

When a child reaches the age of majority, they are required to duel their most direct guardian in a brutal, near‑death contest that ends only when one combatant is permanently marked. The wound is proof the duel is fought for honor, witnessed by the community, and won only when one opponent inflicts a decisive injury on the other. Killing is neither required nor forbidden, but the duel only ends through the submission of one of the fighters due to physical exhaustion. The ritual is proof that the chord of dependency has been severed so that both may now relate as equals.

[[Ballad]]s:

- A gifted [[Spellweaver]] must duel their chronically ill father. Inflicting a permanent wound might kill him, but refusing leaves them legally classified as a child, unable to inherit the magical legacy needed to save their estate. The duel becomes a heart-wrenching dance of pulled punches.

**[[Leylines]] Nomads | Esoteric [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0-III | [[Consonance]]**

Societies that move with the [[Grand Thread Rings]] instead of installing [[Resonance Anchors]] whenever [[Leylines]] move during [[Age Transition]]s, they follow the natural flow of [[Cosmic Motion]] to determine where to establish themselves. Similar to Air Nomads in Avatar.

**[[Sky Glass]] Burials | Esoteric [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0–III | [[Consonance]]**

Funerary and cultural ceremonies involving "sky burying" at the edges of high mountain peaks where [[Sky Glass]] forms naturally. These ceremonies are deeply connected to the tactile, infinite fractals of the glass, and are a reverence to the skies for allowing a sacred passage into the [[Auroral Ribbons]] and [[The Eternal Symphony]].

[[Ballad]]s:

- During a sacred [[Sky Glass]] Burial, the elder is terrified of death and begins spiraling into an [[Atonalis]] to at least have immortality in this state, before he can die the elder hatches into a violent [[Violux]] [[Atonalis]]. The unarmed mourners must use the howling wind and raw [[Resonance]] to push the demon off the cliff without destroying the sacred grounds.

**Chaos Reverence Sacrifices | Esoteric [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0-II | [[Dissonance]]**

Rituals of communal suicide and sacrifice to reverence the chaotic energy that emerges, these societies sacrifice and create suffering to pool [[Formless Masses]] that become revered as "divinity" when they emerge from a [[Dissonance]] Cocoon. This is one of the earliest ways to realize [[We Are Atonalis]], because the emerging [[Atonalis]] is what is being revered as a chaotic entity as divinity due to its anomalous properties made from the collective suffering these societies are ignorant to.

[[Ballad]]s:

- A runaway infiltrates a death cult about to pool enough trauma to birth a [[Fracted]] [[Atonalis]]. Armed only with a [[Resonance Box]], they must disrupt the chanting with a perfectly timed counter-frequency and crash the entire sacrifice ritual before the demon is allowed to hatch from the collective suffering.

### Tier 2 [[Ages]] [[Civic]]s ([[Ages]] IV - VI) ([[Law of Relics]] Established)

### Agromagical, Indulgent, Weaver & Domestication [[Civic]]s

**Cooking Guilds** Evolution of Culinary Alchemists

[[Ballad]]s:

- The grandmaster of a prestigious guild discovers a rival is lacing bread with [[EC]] (Euphoria Compound) as remnants from the [[Great Plague]] to slowly hijack the city guards' nervous systems. Discredited, the grandmaster wages an underground culinary war by creating purifying, anti-toxin meals with the knowledge of [[Vals Jenner]] to break the addiction before a coup occurs.

**Carnival of Shifting Reflections | Indulgent [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VI | [[Cusp]]**

Temporary magical costumes projected by [[Magical Relic]]s that allow participants to become someone else with shapeshifting [[Illusory Magic]]. Any citizen may wear the costume of a ruler, legend, or mythological figure during the [[Ritual Seventh]] of any [[Phase]]. Be it peasant as knight, widow as lost husband. The festival inverts social hierarchy for three days, releasing pressure through playful transformation.

[[Ballad]]s:

- A downtrodden tailor uses an illusion to assume the shape of the city’s ruthless [[Head of State]] to enjoy absolute luxury. The carnival of illusion turns lethal when elite assassins strike thinking he is the real king. Unable to drop the illusion without being executed by the state for treason, the tailor must outwit the killers while maintaining the cruel tyrant persona.

**Polyphonic Choral Singers | Weaver [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VI | [[Consonance]]**

An institution of organized state-managed choral singers of multiple overlayed voices using bells and other [[Magical Relic]]s to enhance the [[Coherence]] of regions. These choruses are versatile and can be used for a variety of applications from agromagical applications to recovery and rebuilding of societies.

[[Ballad]]s:

- A soprano in the royal choir realizes the state is using their complex sheet music to weave a massive Signal Override, erasing the fundamental frequencies of political dissidents. The singer must recruit choristers to secretly weave a counter-melody to shatter the mind-control without breaking harmony.

**Courting Grounds | Weaver [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV | [[Consonance]]**

Evolution of Moonlit Vigil where once per spring, [[Phase of Prelude]], unwed citizens process in a botanical sanctuary beneath the palace gardens. [[Spellweaver]]s in this tradition use their [[Soul Leitmotif]]s to pulse in unison as means to find a partner and conduct rituals of romance and falling in love. Hook: Two rival noble houses both send heirs to the Courts. The heirs resonate—but their families are locked in a blood feud. Romeo & Juliet [[Ballad]].

[[Ballad]]s:

- The heirs of two noble houses locked in a centuries-old blood feud pulse in absolute, flawless unison at the Courting Grounds. State law mandates they marry, forcing the two families into a deadly, covert race to assassinate the opposing heir before the wedding binds their houses. Romeo & Juliet.

**Underground Pleasure Colosseums | Indulgent [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV |  [[Dissonance]]**

Jerez Arena as an evolution of the colosseum [[Civic]]s but focused on slaves gaining freedom but with painful and humiliating dehumanizing punishments on loss. Some of the contracts are directly paired with [[Velvet Nectar]].

### Auric, Trading & Industrious [[Civic]]s

**Memory Markets | Trading [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV–VII | [[Dissonance]]**

Designated economic zones and sites where [[Velvet Nectar]] and its derivations are kept on a zone of exempted legal status and actively traded.

[[Ballad]]s:

- A desperate smuggler steals a vial of [[Velvet Nectar]] to pay a debt, unknowingly consuming the extracted memories of a renowned [[Great Spellweaver]]. Now possessing the dead mage's magical mastery, they are hunted by aristocratic connoisseurs who want the memories back.

**Slave & Servitude Auctions | Trading [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VII | [[Dissonance]]**
Underground trafficking rings with slaves of any species, whether used as commodity, servitude, or livestock.

**[[Contract Arts]] Slavery Guilds [[Dissonance]]**
Using contracts on [[Pure Light]] beings and [[Demi-Human]]s with high enough affinity to be subdued through slave marks as a combination between [[Mind Control Arts]] and [[Contract Arts]] as a perversion of [[Sympathetic Magic]].

### Regal, Militant & Esoteric [[Civic]]s

**Trafficking Rings Conquests | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VII | [[Dissonance]]**
Slavery through subjugated regions that fell due to a slaver causus belly

**Species Caste System | Regal [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VII [[Dissonance]]**
Dividing citizens by tiers of classification depending on their [[Pure Light]] and [[Auric Structure]] between each races of [[Humanity]] and [[Demi-Human]]s.

**Legendary Hunting Charters | Regal [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VII | [[Consonance]]**

When a great beast or [[Atonalis]] threatens a region, the [[Head of State]] issues an open Hunt Charter, a state-sponsored named hunt available to any [[Legend]]. The kill is distributed a hunters council who weigh each participant's contribution, courage, and narrative role. Every charter is inscribed as a civic record, building a living history of who the [[Civilization]] chooses to honor.

[[Ballad]]s:

- An aging, dishonored [[Legend]] takes a near-suicidal hunt to clear their name, only to be ambushed by an arrogant aristocrat trying to steal the kill. When the [[Carnalix]] [[Atonalis]] traps them both in a collapsed ravine built from flesh, the rivals must work together to survive, and vanquish the [[Ascendant]] demon.

**Slayer's Amphitheater | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV–VI | [[Cusp]]**

Public arenas where volunteers, and sometimes prisoners, fight captured [[Atonalis]] before a crowd. Spectators' emotional resonance amplifies the slayer's magic, turning combat into a ritual of communal courage and monster research.

[[Ballad]]s:

- A political [[Spellweaver]] prisoner thrown into the arena against an impossible demon realizes they can manipulate the crowd's roaring emotions. Turning the cheers into a wave of [[Flux]] magic, the prisoner harnesses the collective [[Resonance]] to shatter their magical restraints and incite a bloody rebellion.

**[[Atonalis]] Bombs | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] V Onwards | [[Dissonance]]**

A brutal military tactic inspired by [[Institute]]s where a [[Civilization]] deliberately captures or tortures guilty [[Spellweaver]]s with the explicit intent of forcing their [[Consciousness]] to fracture and collapse into an [[Atonalis]]. These individuals are then sent to infiltrate a rival society as a Trojan horse, inevitably transforming into a destructive demon from inside the walls of an enemy [[Major Settlement]] to cause mass chaos.

[[Ballad]]s:

- A [[Spellweaver]] is tortured into an [[Atonalis]] Bomb and dumped in their own hometown. Feeling their soul cracking and mere hours from hatching into a monster, they must use failing willpower to run as far away from their loved ones as possible, racing to find a wasteland where they can die safely.

**Spiraling Conscription | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV Onwards | [[Dissonance]]**

Inspired by [[Institute]]s, [[Civilization]] utilizes [[Spellweaver]]s who have critically low [[Composure]] as state-sanctioned expedition units. These already half-broken individuals are deliberately deployed into highly hazardous areas, such as [[Vibrational Fallout]] zones and the outer territories of wild magic, gambling on whether the [[Spellweaver]] will break toward an [[Atonalis]] demon or push through the trauma. _"They are already half-broken. The question is whether they break toward the [[Atonalis]] or through it."_

[[Ballad]]s:

- A squad of four highly traumatized conscripts are dropped into wild magic. Instead of breaking, they form an intense level of [[Echoing Bonds]], triggering secondary [[Motif Awakening]]s that make them powerful enough to return to the capital and overthrow the generals who sent them to die.

### Tier 3 [[Ages]] [[Civic]]s ([[Ages]] VII-X)

**Bloodline Tithe | [[Ages]] VII–IX | [[Cusp]]**

Primarily used during the [[Age of Blood]], this [[Civic]] is a systemic tax where noble families must pay the state in blood. The eldest child of a noble house must undergo the Bloodline Tithe, during which a portion of their blood is stored in a family "Hemovault". This accumulated [[Essence Sacrifice]] acts as a familial military battery, drawn upon during wartime to fuel massive [[Civilization]] spells.

- [[Ballad]]s: The eldest daughter of a disgraced noble house goes to offer her blood, only to discover the Hemovault is completely empty. A corrupt government faction has secretly siphoned the generations of [[Essence Sacrifice]] to power an illegal apocalyptic superweapon. Branded a traitor, she must ally with underground [[Void]]-weavers to destroy the weapon before the government drains the life force of every noble family sacrifice made in the empire.

### Tier 4 [[Ages]] [[Civic]]s ([[Ages]] XI-XIV)

Inspired by the polyphonic practices of earlier [[Ages]] this ensemble is unique to the [[Age of Starlight]] using the principle of [[Echoing Bonds]] to establish strong [[Resonance Anchors]] within its cast of [[Spellweaver]]s through [[Harmonic Entanglement]].

### The [[Ballad]]s of [[Civilization]] [[Civic]]s

**Early Civilization and Classical Ages (Ages 0 - III)**

**The Ballad of the Starving Symphony | Culinary Alchemists (Agromagical Civic)**

- **The Lore:** This civic involves practical magical cooking where local ingredients are communally shared and recorded in a "Flavor Log" to create temporary enhancements to spellweaving.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A dedicated but untalented chef in a starving settlement discovers an ancient, bloodstained page torn from their ancestors' Flavor Log. The recipe promises a meal that can perfectly stabilize the psychological Composure of the entire village, but it requires a rare ingredient found only deep within a Vibrational Fallout zone. The chef must convince a traumatized, half-broken Spellweaver to escort them into the deadly anomaly, turning a simple foraging mission into a desperate struggle for the settlement's survival.

**The [[Ballad]] of Hollow Banquet | Feast of Abundance (Indulgent Civic)**

- **The Lore:** A mandatory wealth redistribution festival where surplus goods and Auric Peaches are thrown to the public. Hoarding wealth is heavily taxed, and Legends who give the most earn high social legitimacy.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A manipulative aristocrat plots to seize the title of Head of State without shedding a single drop of blood. By secretly hoarding vast amounts of wealth in hidden Void-pockets to avoid the hoarding tax, they plan a massive, unprecedented distribution at the Feast of Abundance to instantly buy the absolute loyalty of the populace. An undercover Justiciar discovers the plot and must race against time to expose the economic sabotage before the feast crowns a tyrant.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Traitor's Ink | Ballad & Fantasy Plays (Weaver Civic)**

- **The Lore:** State-sanctioned guilds of writers, singers, and composers tasked with creating culture and preserving the ballads of Legends, officially patronized by the classical civilization of Iridia.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A state-sponsored playwright tasked with writing a propagandist fantasy play accidentally uncovers a Scorching Truth while researching the empire's founding Legend—discovering that the hero was actually a cowardly deserter. Knowing the Auric Order executes anyone holding forbidden knowledge, the playwright decides to encode the dark truth into the very script of the play, sparking a tense psychological thriller of censorship, art, and treason right under the king's nose.

**The [[Ballad]] of Severed Winds | Ritual Whistling Fans Dancers (Weaver Civic)**

- **The Lore:** Cultural and martial ceremonies patronizing the arts of dance and combat, inspired by Sephira, the Mythic Virtuoso of Cindergale.
- **The Narrative Hook:** During the grandest martial ceremony of the decade, a young dancer realizes that their rival's Whistling Fans have been secretly tuned to a Dissonant frequency. Every movement the rival makes is designed to slowly shatter the protagonist's internal Coherence and trigger a mid-performance panic attack. The dancer must adapt their choreography on the fly, fighting a deadly acoustic battle disguised as a beautiful, synchronized duet.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Locked Love | Moonlit Vigil (Weaver Civic)**

- **The Lore:** A silent courtship ritual held in Glimmerfern groves during a full Moon, where individuals attempt to naturally find a matching emotional frequency with a partner without speaking.
- **The Narrative Hook:** The heir to a powerful noble house sneaks into a peasant Moonlit Vigil and unexpectedly phase-locks in perfect Sympathetic Vibration with a commoner, falling deeply in love. When the noble family discovers the bond, they demand the heir undergo a loveless political marriage instead. The story becomes a tragic, high-stakes romance where the couple must decide whether to sever their true magical connection or trigger a civil war to protect their Resonance.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Crystal Stampede | The Ball Fluff Runs & Horned Flag Stampedes (Domestication Civics)**

- **The Lore:** Dangerous public arena events involving giant sticky fluff balls or bull-like Pure Light creatures with Crystal-tipped horns. Survivors who collect the most flags or finish the run win a grand feast or domesticated produce.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A disgraced former knight enters the deadly Horned Flag Stampede simply to win a feast for a group of starving orphans. However, as the gates open, they realize a conspirator in the crowd has cast a polyrhythmic spell to frenzy the Crystal-horned beasts, turning a dangerous game into an outright massacre. The knight must drop their weapons and use only their wits and evasive maneuvers to protect the other runners from the maddened creatures.

**The [[Ballad]] of Painted [[Composure]] | Truth Soul Leitmotif Testimonies (Regal Civic)**

- **The Lore:** A legal practice requiring individuals to expose the dormant state of their Soul Leitmotif (the Resting Egg) when signing social contracts. Because the dormant gem reflects absolute emotional truth, it acts as a flawless lie detector.
- **The Narrative Hook:** An infamous spy has infiltrated the highest echelons of a rival empire and is about to frame the signing a monumental peace treaty that will secretly doom the nation. Knowing they must expose their Soul Leitmotif during the ceremony, the spy utilizes forbidden Illusory Magic—bending Luminance to project a false aura of Pristine Composure over their deeply corrupted, treacherous soul. While framing the head of state of tyranny. A low-ranking clerk notices a microscopic flicker of Dissonance and must prove the deception before the ink dries and a war begins.

**The [[Ballad]] of Fracture Quorum | Harmonic Quorum (Regal Civic)**

- **The Lore:** A democratic governance system where policies can only pass if the assembled leadership attunes their internal Coherence to a single frequency via Sympathetic Vibration. If there is doubt or conflict, the policy fails.
- **The Narrative Hook:** The council has exactly one hour to pass a desperate military edict to deploy a shield against an encroaching Atonalis swarm. However, the Harmonic Quorum keeps failing because one hidden council member is secretly terrified and generating Discordant Interference. The protagonist must use their Strand and Luminance bindings to interrogate the minds of the council, hunting down the invisible coward before the demons breach the city walls.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Conquerors Vow | Bridal Conquest (Militant Civic)**

- **The Lore:** A martial and diplomatic practice where conquering forces capture enemy rulers or high-ranking knights to marry them into their own empire, securing strong magical lineages and unifying cultures.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A proud, undefeated warlord is captured and forced into a Bridal Conquest with the empress who decimated their homeland. Over years of political maneuvering and forced proximity, the two fierce enemies develop a genuine, undeniable Resonance that surprises them both. But just as they finally admit their love, the warlord's former generals breach the capital to "rescue" them and assassinate the empress, forcing the warlord to turn against their own people to protect their captor.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Echoing Hunt | Grand Hunts of Legends (Militant Civic)**

- **The Lore:** State-sponsored tracking parties of elite Spellweavers deployed to hunt high-ranking Atonalis demons and Pure Light Behemoths, forging permanent synergy bonds among the hunters.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A legendary hunting party tracks an ancient, elusive [[Ascendant]] [[Atonalis]] into a collapsed mountain pass. During the hunt, the team's tracker realizes the monster is perfectly anticipating their tactics because the demon is the corrupted, shattered Soul Leitmotif of their original mentor. The hunt devolves into psychological horror as the demon uses their shared memories to turn the hunters against one another.

**The [[Ballad]] of Gentle Severance | Duels of Severance (Militant Civic)**

- **The Lore:** A coming-of-age ritual involving a brutal duel with a guardian that ends only when a permanent wound is inflicted, proving the child has become an equal and severing the chord of dependency.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A young, exceptionally gifted Spellweaver must face their aging, chronically ill father in the Duel of Severance. The protagonist knows that inflicting a permanent wound might accidentally kill the frail man, but refusing to strike will leave them legally classified as a child forever, unable to inherit the family's magical legacy to save their estate. The duel becomes a heart-wrenching dance of pulled punches and desperate strategy.

**The [[Ballad]] of a Shattered Sky | Leylines Nomads & Sky Glass Burials (Esoteric Civics)**

- **The Lore:** Nomadic societies that migrate with the natural flow of Cosmic Motion rather than building Resonance Anchors, practicing funerary "sky burying" at mountain peaks to honor the dead's passage into the Auroral Ribbons.
- **The Narrative Hook:** During a sacred Sky Glass Burial atop the highest peak in Arcanoria, a nomadic tribe watches in horror as the deceased elder's soul does not pass peacefully into the Auroral Ribbons. Instead, driven by a secret, unconfessed guilt, the elder's spirit cracks and hatches into a violent Violux Atonalis. Trapped on the edge of a cliff, the unarmed mourners must use the howling wind and raw Resonance to push the demon off the mountain without destroying the sacred burial grounds.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Silenced Savior | Chaos Reverence Sacrifices (Esoteric Civic)**

- **The Lore:** Dark rituals of communal suicide and suffering designed to pool Formless Masses, inadvertently birthing and worshiping Atonalis demons as chaotic divinities.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A skeptical runaway infiltrates a death cult on the eve of their grand Chaos Reverence Sacrifice. The cult believes they are summoning a savior god through mass suffering, but the protagonist knows they are merely pooling enough trauma to birth an apocalyptic [[Ascendant]] [[Atonalis]]. Armed with only a Resonance Box, the protagonist must disrupt the communal chanting with a perfectly timed counter-frequency before the demon hatches.

**The Medieval Ages (Ages IV – VI)**

**The [[Ballad]] of the Poisoned Dough | Cooking Guilds (Agromagical Civic)**

- **The Lore:** The highly institutionalized evolution of the early Culinary Alchemists.
- **The Narrative Hook:** The grandmaster of the city’s most prestigious Cooking Guild discovers a conspiracy: a rival guild is lacing their bread with synthesized Euphoria Compounds to slowly hijack the nervous systems of the city guard. Stripped of their rank and discredited, the grandmaster must wage an underground culinary war, creating purifying, anti-toxin meals to break the addiction before the rival guild initiates a coup.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Painted King | Carnival of Shifting Reflections (Indulgent Civic)**

- **The Lore:** A three-day festival where citizens use Illusory Magic relics to wear temporary magical costumes, completely inverting social hierarchies.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A downtrodden, indebted tailor uses an Illusory relic during the Carnival to assume the shape of the city’s ruthless Head of State, intending to enjoy three days of absolute luxury. The prank turns lethal when a cabal of assassins strikes, believing the tailor is the real tyrant. Unable to drop the illusion without being executed by the state for treason, the tailor must outwit elite killers while maintaining the persona of the cruelest person in the empire.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Subversive Soprano | Polyphonic Choral Singers (Weaver Civic)**

- **The Lore:** State-managed choirs that overlay multiple voices using bells and relics to actively enhance regional Coherence.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A newly recruited soprano in the royal Polyphonic Choir realizes that the complex sheet music they are performing is slightly off. The state isn't using the choir to stabilize Coherence; they are weaving a massive, city-wide Signal Override to erase the fundamental frequencies of political dissidents. The singer must recruit other choristers to secretly weave a counter-melody of Cindergale and Strand into their performances to shatter the state's mind-control without breaking harmony.

**The [[Ballad]] of a Bleeding Unison Love | Courting Grounds (Weaver Civic)**

- **The Lore:** Unwed citizens process in botanical sanctuaries and use their Soul Leitmotifs to pulse in unison to find a partner. The lore specifically highlights a Romeo & Juliet hook.
- **The Narrative Hook:** Two rival noble houses, locked in a brutal, centuries-old blood feud, send their heirs to the Courting Grounds to find strategic political matches. To the horror of both families, the two heirs' Soul Leitmotifs pulse in absolute, flawless unison. The state law mandates that such a perfect Resonance must be honored with marriage, forcing the two warring families into a deadly, covert race to assassinate the opposing heir before the wedding binds their houses forever.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Velvet Ghost | Memory Markets (Trading Civic)**

- **The Lore:** Designated economic zones with exempted legal status where highly addictive Velvet Nectar—distilled from extracted memories and suffering—is actively traded.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A desperate smuggler in the Memory Markets steals a highly prized vial of Velvet Nectar to pay off a debt, unaware that the vial contains the extracted memories of a murdered Great Spellweaver. Upon accidentally consuming a drop, the smuggler inherits the dead mage's memories and magical mastery. Now hunted by the aristocratic connoisseurs of the Velvet Market who want the memories back, the smuggler must master their new, terrifying powers to survive the night.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Fleshy Mountain Pass | Legendary Hunting Charters (Regal Civic)**

- **The Lore:** Open, state-sponsored hunts for great beasts or Atonalis. The kill is distributed by a council and inscribed as a civic record, bringing immense prestige.
- **The Narrative Hook:** An aging, dishonored Legend takes up a near-suicidal Hunting Charter against a colossal Carnalix to clear their name and secure a civic record for their impoverished family. During the hunt, they are ambushed by a younger, arrogant aristocrat who plans to steal the kill. The two rivals are forced to work together when they realize the beast has trapped them both in a collapsed ravine, turning the hunt for glory into a gritty fight for survival.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Roaring Wards | Slayer's Amphitheater (Militant Civic)**

- **The Lore:** Public arenas where volunteers or prisoners fight captured Atonalis. The spectators' emotional resonance actively amplifies the slayer's magic.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A political prisoner is thrown into the Slayer's Amphitheater against an impossible Discant demon. As the fight drags on, the prisoner realizes they can manipulate the crowd's roaring emotions, turning the spectators' cheers into a massive wave of Flux magic. The prisoner decides not just to kill the demon, but to harness the amphitheater's collective Resonance to shatter the magical wards holding them captive and incite a bloody arena rebellion.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Exile's Sprint | Atonalis Bombs (Militant Civic)**

- **The Lore:** A brutal tactic where guilty Spellweavers are tortured until their consciousness shatters, then sent as Trojan horses into rival settlements to transform into destructive demons from within.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A devoted spellweaver is captured by an enemy Institute and subjected to unspeakable psychological torture to turn them into an Atonalis Bomb. Dumped in the center of their own hometown, they can feel their Soul Leitmotif cracking, mere hours away from hatching into a monstrous Primal Discordia. The spellweaver must use every ounce of their failing Crystal willpower to run far away from the people they love, racing against their own collapsing mind to find a wasteland where they can die without hurting anyone.

**The [[Ballad]] of the Broken Vanguard | Spiraling Conscription (Militant Civic)**

- **The Lore:** The state-sanctioned deployment of half-broken Spellweavers with critically low Composure into highly hazardous Vibrational Fallout zones, gambling on whether they will push through their trauma or shatter into an Atonalis.
- **The Narrative Hook:** A squad of four "Spiraling" conscripts—all suffering from extreme PTSD and hovering on the edge of demonic transformation—are dropped into a terrifying zone of wild magic. Instead of breaking, the squad forms an intense, desperate Echoing Bond. Together, they must navigate the fallout zone, using their shared trauma not to become monsters, but to trigger secondary Motif Awakenings and return to the capital powerful enough to overthrow the generals who sent them to die.

**Enlightenment and Reformation Ages (Ages VII – IX)**

**The [[Ballad]] of the Empty Hemovault | Bloodline Tithe (Regal/Militant Civic)**

- **The Lore:** A systemic tax where noble families must store their blood in a "Hemovault." This accumulated Essence Sacrifice serves as a massive military battery drawn upon during wartime.
- **The Narrative Hook:** The eldest daughter of a disgraced noble house prepares to offer her blood to the state's Hemovault, only to discover the vault is completely empty. A corrupt faction of the government has been secretly siphoning the nobility's generational Essence Sacrifice to power an illegal, apocalyptic superweapon. Branded a traitor for discovering the truth, the daughter must ally with an underground faction of Void-weavers to break into the capital and destroy the weapon before the government drains the life force of every noble family in the empire.

entries.title: Coherence
entries.summary: How likely something is to exist, it is the contrary of chaos and [[Primal White Noise]]. Giving [[Coherence]] to the [[Known Universe]] is the primary objective of both the [[Auric Heptacode]] and the [[Trinity Harmony]]. It's a fundamental part of [[Spellweaving]] as well as it is the basis of [[Absolute Certainty]].
entries.body:
How likely something is to exist, it is the contrary of chaos and [[Primal White Noise]]. Giving [[Coherence]] to the [[Known Universe]] is the primary objective of both the [[Auric Heptacode]] and the [[Trinity Harmony]]. It's a fundamental part of [[Spellweaving]] as well as it is the basis of [[Absolute Certainty]].

High [[Coherence]] forms [[Stable Harmonic Channels]] for information and magical transit through the [[Great Harmonic Loom]].

[[Coherence]] is not the absence of chaos, but rather a pattern so profound it can maintain integrity even at the edge of total dissolution.

entries.title: Composure
entries.summary: The level of stress, sanity, and meter of the internal [[Coherence]] of any [[Spellweaver]].
entries.body:
The level of stress, sanity, and meter of the internal [[Coherence]] of any [[Spellweaver]].

To lose [[Composure]] is to lose oneself, if all [[Composure]] is lost at the level of surrender, the [[Soul Leitmotif]] fractures, enveloping the [[Spellweaver]] in pure [[Dissonance]].

When the cocoon hatches in a wave of [[Discordant Interference]], what walks out is an [[Atonalis]], no longer a person nor [[Spellweaver]] but a broken hungry husk permanently trapped in the torturing paradox of an existence without [[Coherence]].

Thus, [[Composure]] is the most important metric for any [[Spellweaver]], it is visible in the [[Soul Leitmotif]] as it gets cloudy with muddy black [[Dissonance]] that becomes blacker and cloudier the closer a [[Spellweaver]] is to surrender and [[Corruption]].

[[Composure]] consists of 5 stress levels on the [[Soul Leitmotif]] that mirror that of the growth phases of an [[Atonalis]] from [[Nascent]] to [[Primal Discordia]]:

- Pristine: The perfect rest state for a [[Soul Leitmotif]], it is vibrant in color, beautiful, and emits light with the color of its primary binding. Usually represents a peaceful and [[Consonance]] filled state of mind. Momentarily, a [[Soul Leitmotif]] can become pristine on intense moments of joy.
- Clouded: This is the normal state for most [[Spellweaver]]s, it has the vibrant light of the primary binding but certain parts of the inside of the gem have black [[Dissonance]] which gives it the primary color a clouded view of the interior structure, it doesn't look translucid as a Pristine state, but it doesn't have physical damage. Despite being murky, this state is usually where a [[Spellweaver]] acts with most confidence, mirroring that of [[Sectile]] [[Atonalis]] where they have rationalized enough their own wound to be fully functional but without the awareness necessary to cripple them in their own despair. [[Formless Masses]]
- Fractured: This is the first sign of actual damage to the [[Soul Leitmotif]], black cracks appear visible in the outer casing, not just on the inside cloudiness anymore. This state is necessary for triggering a [[Motif Awakening]] as the seeping cracks allow the [[Soul Leitmotif]] to adopt and embellish new [[Ornament]]s from the created space within. It is healthy, and almost inevitable, for a [[Spellweaver]] to reach this state but it's key to remember that any wound is merely a source of power, and what gives power can also crack you open. If the wound continues to fester it's a dangerous pivot to surrendering oneself.
- Spiraling: This is the final level before the point of no return, and it has a signature of black fractal spirals that begin to mirror the own internal chaos of the [[Spellweaver]] that is falling to the abyss of despair. The spirals on the surface are similar to [[Sky Glass]] but devoid of its beautiful tactile qualities, and this is the closest state that a [[Spellweaver]] can be to becoming an [[Atonalis]] before falling to the point of no return. **This is the last point where anyone can intervene to save them.** Any breach further on the hungering fractal spirals and the [[Soul Leitmotif]] will undergo its permanent transformation when it is fully consumed by the black of the [[Dissonance]], turning itself into a [[Dissonance Core]].
- Surrender: Once a [[Soul Leitmotif]] reaches this point, there's nothing anyone can do to save them. It has a clear indicator of two distinct crack sounds, the first is when the threshold is reached, when the [[Soul Leitmotif]] went beyond its maximum stress point, and the [[Spellweaver]] is on its last remnants of [[Coherence]] that tether their [[Composure]]. The second crack is the inevitable moment when the [[Spellweaver]] vocalizes their last words. Upon reaching this state the [[Dissonance]] cocoon emerges siphoning the user inside of it, transforming the [[Soul Leitmotif]] into the very [[Dissonance Core]] of the [[Atonalis]]. The location of the [[Dissonance Core]] is often the Wearable State of the soul gem in the last moment the dying [[Consciousness]] assigned value to anything. **The refusal to process pain feels exactly like mercy right up until the moment it permanently turns you into a predator.**

The state of the [[Soul Leitmotif]] [[Composure]] directly aligns with the internal state of mind of the [[Spellweaver]]:

A Pristine State of Mind, a Clouded State of Mind, a Fractured State of Mind, a Spiraling State of Mind, and the Surrendered State of Mind.

Despite the visual cues, these are only visible during the resting state of the [[Soul Leitmotif]]. If it's on the Wearable State, none of the Clouded or Pristine levels are visible, the only moment the [[Dissonance]] is visible on a non resting state is only until the [[Spellweaver]]'s [[Composure]] reaches Spiraling or below, and it will become visible as [[Discordant Interference]] pulsing with flickering dark alongside the color of whichever binding they're channeling.

Any real deity, like the [[Auric Aria]] or [[Outer God]]s can't become [[Atonalis]]. However, they do require [[Composure]] to function. This is particularly notable in the [[Auric Aria]] which did reach the surrender point during the [[Eighth Cycle]] and provoked the [[Lost Cycle]] for uncountable [[Cycle]]s. Her eventual return due to the pleas of [[Humanity]]gave her a sliver of [[Composure]] to move from spiraling into recovery to clouded Golden Sovereign of the [[Old Testament]].

The [[Auric Aria]] has only reached the surrendered state once, and on its very border which is why she came back to creation. Only does in the [[Alternate Hollowing]] she fully embraces the surrendered state and triggers the end of the [[Known Universe]] back into static. Typically, she hovers between spiraling at her worst, fractured on a regular, and clouded at her most vivid. Only after the sequence of the [[Singer of Paradise]], and in the apex of the [[Parlor of the Moon]] does she attain Pristine [[Composure]] after reconciliation with [[Selenea]] in the end of the [[Sonata]] of [[Arcanoria]].

### Societal Implications

Due to the [[Composure]] meter reflecting the internal state of mind of a [[Spellweaver]], there are several layers of implications on how this information is shared, externalized, or even weaponized through relationships, and even diplomacy.

Usually the sacredness of sharing the inner view of the [[Soul Leitmotif]] is considered a moment of vulnerability, which is precisely why it's mostly equipped in the wearable state and only transformed into the resting version due to forced exhaustion, sleep, or sacred meditation. It's uncommon to have a [[Soul Leitmotif]] in a resting state without a personal guard of sorts, and it's impossible to do so without consent unless the [[Spellweaver]] physically passes out.

Even travelling parties or with allies the [[Spellweaver]] tends to keep in secret their dormant [[Soul Leitmotif]] whether in a pocket or directly by clutching it somewhere in their body during sleep. (Like hiding money under the pillow)

Furthermore, this also extends to a personal level for relationships. To deliberately invite someone to see the inside of your soul is a deeply personal and intimate gesture of courtship and romance between [[Spellweaver]]s, and in some cultures the exposure of the bare soul is indistinct from showing a naked body, which makes by proxy the dormant state as sacred as the act of physical intimacy, and to some degree both can be intertwined.

On a societal level this also reflects in diplomacy, where envoys most often than not tend to be non [[Spellweaver]]s, as [[Humanity]] without a [[Soul Leitmotif]] is useful precisely to keep undercover the internal state during the negotiations. Even if there's a [[Spellweaver]] present, most notably with any [[Head of State]], they tend to use it on the Wearable State as both class, clothing, and as means to prevent the visualization of their internal state of [[Coherence]].

However, there are some cultures that do require honesty as means to establish any formal treaty, this type of society tends to align with the [[Aureus Pillar]] or [[Waltz Pillar]]s, and they present negotiations through a pedestal where the dormant "sacred" state of a [[Soul Leitmotif]] is an anchor to the truthfulness of both parties, sometimes this technique is required in unethical practices such as torture or court trial to get information that prevents perjury due to the microscopic flashes of the [[Soul Leitmotif]] and its relationship to the [[Key of Attunement]].

This later half however does not mean a [[Spellweaver]] can't lie, on the contrary, this very basis of informational manipulation is a core tenet of [[Illusory Magic]], to bend the [[Luminance]] of a [[Soul Leitmotif]] to deliberately guide, frame, blackmail or create false evidence. The race of [[Illusory Magic]] is similar to the [[Strand]] [[Detective Magic]] applications, creating a loop of [[Spellweaving]] mastery of having measures to lie and counter measures to detect lies.

This very principle on [[Illusory Magic]] is one of the great contributions to [[The Principles of Magic]] by the partnership of [[Luminaire]] and [[Amadea]], the respective [[Mythical Virtuoso]]s of [[Luminance]] and [[Void]], the partnership gets even pushed further with [[Cordelia]] making the intersection of these [[Mythical Virtuoso]] the founding school of proper [[Illusory Magic]] and [[Detective Magic]].

The implications of having a visual cue to the [[Soul Leitmotif]] is both important religion, diplomacy, and culture wise, heavily varying on the interpretation of the [[Pillars]] of [[Civilization]]. Lying becomes much more sophisticated and hard to identify if the evidence itself can be contradictory.
entries.source: Worldbuilding/Origin of Magic/Spellweaving/Composure.md

entries.title: Consciousness
entries.epigraph: *The ink which writes [[The Eternal Symphony]]*.
entries.summary: An abstract form of raw existence, it is one of the most essential concepts for giving form into matter and energy from chaos, thus [[Mastery Over Chaos]] being the principal method of transforming reality.
entries.body:
An abstract form of raw existence, it is one of the most essential concepts for giving form into matter and energy from chaos, thus [[Mastery Over Chaos]] being the principal method of transforming reality.

It exists in all of [[The Infinite Void]], and emerges as a variation of it as a structured deterministic pattern in [[The First Overtone]]. Ironically, it is a diluted version of [[Primal White Noise]] that has stabilized into existence as a [[Fundamental Frequency]].

Crystalized [[Consciousness]] is the primary element of [[Crystal]] and reflects this as the laws of quantum collapse in the [[Auric Heptacode]].
entries.source: Worldbuilding/Origin of Magic/Conduits of Magic/Consciousness.md

entries.title: Consensual Anchoring
entries.epigraph: _"That wall is, in fact, invisible" - [[Puppet Master]] [[Luminance]] [[Spellweaver]]_
entries.summary: A delusion can sustain [[Signal Loss]] if you can exchange which [[Consciousness]] believes in the spell. This is a [[Crystal]] / [[Luminance]] / [[Flux]] interaction where [[Stable Harmonic Channels]] form if the caster can deceive or force the target to also believe the illusion is real.
entries.body:
A delusion can sustain [[Signal Loss]] if you can exchange which [[Consciousness]] believes in the spell. This is a [[Crystal]] / [[Luminance]] / [[Flux]] interaction where [[Stable Harmonic Channels]] form if the caster can deceive or force the target to also believe the illusion is real.

It is a funding principle of [[Illusory Magic]] that says that combat is as much of a battle of technical mastery and sheer imagination as it is of psychological dominance.

**Narrative Applications:**

- A city where everyone believes a lie—the lie becomes true
- An illusionist who's gathered a cult to make their illusions permanent
- The horror of realizing your own disbelief is _hurting_ someone—if you stop believing in their protective illusion, it fails

entries.title: Constellation
entries.epigraph: _"Death is just the day of the publication of your [[Magnum Opus]]."_
entries.summary: A [[Legend]] that has ascended to the [[Stellar Legacy Score]]. They can form a variety of [[Stellar Covenant]]s. [[Outer God]]s and actual deities can't be [[Constellation]]s, they have to be [[Legend]]s exclusively.
entries.body:
A [[Legend]] that has ascended to the [[Stellar Legacy Score]]. They can form a variety of [[Stellar Covenant]]s. [[Outer God]]s and actual deities can't be [[Constellation]]s, they have to be [[Legend]]s exclusively.

All [[Constellation]]s live in a spectrum between [[Constellation]]s of [[Consonance]] and [[Constellation]]s of [[Dissonance]]. This alignment depends on whether they were "good" or "evil" during their lifetime as a [[Legend]]. The specific alignment depends on the type of [[Legend Opus]] and [[Legend Title]]s they have:

- [[Constellation]] of pure [[Consonance]]: [[Mira]] given that they were pretty selfless in their life, and did genuine good for those dying while she herself suffered the same condition. Her offer to [[Lacrimosa]] was also born from a place of [[Consonance]].
- [[Constellation]] of pure [[Dissonance]]: [[Syvanth]] which is the complete opposite as his [[Legend]] came to be born as the Killer of the Great Expanse and whose [[Legend]] is the ominous [[Ballad]] sung after his horrific beautification.
- Mixture of [[Consonance]] and [[Dissonance]]: [[Cadmus Tacet]] which is a complex moral character as he had great [[Legend Opus]] like the Scalpel of [[Humanity]]'s Hope, but also horrific [[Legend Title]]s due to the means he used to achieve said goals, like The Vivisector due to his brutal methods on mapping the [[Pure Light]] spectrum. Most [[Constellation]]s are placed in this bracket as a mixture of both.

Depending on the specific pairings on which [[Constellation]]s are receiving [[Constellation Worship]], they can unlock several effects, and the mixture between [[Consonance]] and [[Dissonance]] is a fertile ground for friction and unique [[Syncretism]]. Furthermore, [[Constellation]]s can change their affinity to either [[Consonance]] or [[Dissonance]] through [[Mythic Drift]] by adapting to the new ways on which they receive their specific [[Constellation Worship]].

Finally, [[Constellation]]s of great [[Constellation Renown]] and [[Constellation Worship]] can have the ability of [[Reincarnation]] due to having a strong tether between [[Arcanoria]] and [[The Eternal Symphony]]. This allows a character to be reborn in [[Ages]] different from the ones in their original mythos. They receive some bonus to their starting [[Legend Trait]]s based on their defining [[Constellation]], but are effectively "reset" of all their memories and previous titles. They are a blank canvas that shares the same character [[Soul-Key]] and name, considering both their original starting [[Legend Trait]]s and physical looks. They are back the moment before they began their original [[Legend]]. Moreover, some [[Dissonance]] [[Legend Trait]]s can be removed of their origin to accommodate to a new life. For example, removing "Orphan" from [[Mira]] since she has an actual family now.

[[Reincarnation]] can only be triggered after the [[Constellation]] has experienced at least three [[Ages]] being a [[Constellation]]. Furthermore, the process itself is costly and requires a strong tether of [[Resonance]] between [[Arcanoria]] and [[The Eternal Symphony]]. Thus, [[Reincarnation]] can only happen during an [[Age Transition]], and its dependent on the slots [[Civilization]] has unlocked for [[Reincarnation]]. The default state is up to two concurrent [[Reincarnation]]s but after learning [[The Truth of Arcanoria]] the slots can be expanded and its cooldowns of three [[Ages]] can be reduced.
entries.source: Worldbuilding/Society/Stellar Legacy/Constellation.md

entries.title: Cordelia
entries.summary: The [[Mythical Virtuoso]] of [[Strand]] of the Seven Virtuosi.
entries.body:
The [[Mythical Virtuoso]] of [[Strand]] of the Seven Virtuosi.

[[Legend Title]]: The Panacea, Mother of All Healers, The Time Bender, Saint Patron of [[Great Chronicler]]s, The Hollowed Miracle Maker.

[[Primary Instrument]]: [[Own Voice]], Threaded Lyre Harp
[[Armament]]:
[[Soul Leitmotif]]: [[Strand]]
[[Ornament]]s: [[Flux]], [[Cindergale]]

Evolution of Moonlit Vigil where once per spring, [[Phase of Prelude]], unwed citizens process in a botanical sanctuary beneath the palace gardens. [[Spellweaver]]s in this tradition use their [[Soul Leitmotif]]s to pulse in unison as means to find a partner and conduct rituals of romance and falling in love. Hook: Two rival noble houses both send heirs to the Courts. The heirs resonate—but their families are locked in a blood feud. Romeo & Juliet [[Ballad]].

[[Ballad]]s:

- The heirs of two noble houses locked in a centuries-old blood feud pulse in absolute, flawless unison at the Courting Grounds. State law mandates they marry, forcing the two families into a deadly, covert race to assassinate the opposing heir before the wedding binds their houses. Romeo & Juliet.

entries.title: Crescent Mist Peaks
entries.epigraph: _"The Throne of the Heavens, for anyone suicidal or fool enough that doesn't die trying to reach the apex of its glory."_
entries.summary: The [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] are a [[Landmark]], biome and key religious location of high [[Vibrational Density]] in the upper layers. They are a contradiction of [[Sky Glass]] and waterfalls carved into the sky, forming an idyllic wound in the world's highest spine, as beautiful as it is lethal.
entries.body:
The [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] are a [[Landmark]], biome and key religious location of high [[Vibrational Density]] in the upper layers. They are a contradiction of [[Sky Glass]] and waterfalls carved into the sky, forming an idyllic wound in the world's highest spine, as beautiful as it is lethal. They are amongst the highest peaks in [[Arcanoria]], and hold the clearest view of the [[Grand Thread Rings]] of all [[Landmark]]s.

**Three Laws govern all who enter:**

_The Mist Remembers:_ The silver mist is a sort of vaporized [[Lunehymn]], carrying fragmented dreams of every pilgrim who has climbed before. Prolonged exposure is to risk experiencing someone else's death as vivid hallucinations.

_The Mountain Dreams in Fractals:_ The [[Sky Glass]] formations are not random. They are the mountain's dream-logic made visible, the same recursive pattern repeating at every scale, from frost [[Crystal]]s to the arrangement of the peaks themselves.

_The Abyss Listens:_ The [[Lunar Abyss]] is not empty. It is receptive. Sound carries downward without decay, and anything shouted into the chasm returns transformed, as though something below has answered in a language that only resembles the original words.

The location is sacred to both the [[Aureus Pillar]] and the [[Chorus Pillar]] but for different reasons, it is a marvel of [[Auric Geometry]] and it is a sanctuary of [[Lunehymn]] and dream-like states necessary for [[Outer God]] communion.

The location itself is composed of several mountain valleys that grind jagged fangs of veined granite and black ice that rise in the shape of crescents and arched pass ways above a frozen wasteland that never fully surrenders to winter. Amidst the impossible terrain there are several waterfalls that pour not into rivers but through veins of [[Sky Glass]] that flow upward as visible ribbons of fractals behind translucent stone before spilling from cliff lips in thin white curtains that dissolve long before reaching ground.

The [[Sky Glass]] itself forms in layered shelves across the highest plateaus, simultaneously delicate in appearance and impossible to shatter, its surface fractal-threaded with the frozen geometry of dendrites, spiraling forms, and snowflake architectures repeating at every scale. The mountain is said to be quietly demonstrating the same pattern at every magnification, forever.

**The [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] do not offer wisdom, power, or salvation. They offer only friction and the resistance that forces pilgrims to become more than they were.**

Culturally, they are a place of "do or die" for anyone seeking a deep understanding of oneself. These are the idyllic places that create or break a person anew. It is one of the most profound personal journeys in [[Arcanoria]]. Its structure is divided by height into these core regions:

- [[Sky Glass]] Ascent: The uppermost zone and accessible by very few, the [[Grand Thread Rings]] entire structure of its [[Fractal Kaleidoscope]]s is seen at every layer of the ascent. In the [[Strand Pool]]s, the clearest [[Sky Glass]] forms in layered shelves. [[Coherence]] is at its peak here, but so is exposure. It is filled with towers, ramps, galleries and stairs of ice, raised and spun with the architecture of dreams. The air thins, and spells cast at this altitude risk triggering a localized [[Chaotic Resonant Cascade]] that can shatter the nearby [[Sky Glass]] formations and changing the topology of entire passes. The internal corridors of the ascent change continuously making it mandatory to carry a [[Resonance Stabilizer]] and a [[Celestial Astrolabe]] to guide the path.
- Whispering Gallery: Rows of natural amphitheaters carved with perfect acoustics. Very jagged fractal shapes with both high and low [[Coherence]] which tend to make [[Spellweaving]] unreliable. The inner galleries shift quickly in topology. Here, a whisper at one end can be heard clearly at the other — it is said that the mountain answers. This is the typical end of pilgrimages. Legend holds that when a pilgrim speaks their original [[Motif Awakening]] Wish aloud, the Gallery answers: if the root of fulfilling your wish lies in the future, the sound rings in [[Consonance]] as a sign to press onward. If it lies in the past, [[Discordant Interference]] shatters the sound as a sign to turn inward, to fix what has not yet been resolved. If drinking concentrated [[Lunehymn]], it is also possible to ask the mountain questions about the own's unconscious and the [[Consonance]] or [[Dissonance]] reply back as a yes or a no, which makes it useful for [[Piety]] and Revelation for oneself.
- Crescent Veils: Mist-shrouded ridges, glacial terraces, twilight-blooming frost flowers with zones of high [[Coherence]] and [[Leylines]] converging. The mist here is thickest; it is also the most dangerous. Breathing it too long induces [[Lunehymn]] Narcosis that induce the vivid hallucinations of past pilgrims' deaths, forcing you to relive their final moments regardless of where these occurred, this is the maximum point the [[Lunehymn]] mist touches, and it has a lot of [[Aetherlight]] rays that collide with one another nullifying the ascent of more mist.
- Silver Cascades: The Upper Habitable Zone, primarily for [[Secluded Refuge]]s and [[Sacred Site]]s. The name stems from the [[Lunehymn]] waterfalls threading through [[Sky Glass]], in visible fractal light mirroring stained glass with iridescent flickers. These zones are known for having [[Time Bubble]]s, identifiable by reflections hanging suspended in the cloudy ice. While most of them are visible as actual bubbles that go upward with the cascades, some of them are large enough that a person can get trapped into the [[Time Bubble]] experiencing the normal phenomenon within these [[Strand Pool]]s.
- Boreal Reach: The Lower Habitable Zone and Entry to the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]]. The characteristic trees and [[Glimmerfern]] fronds give its signature name. On the upward ascent, when almost reaching the silver cascades, the trails become deliberately misleading, with switchbacks double back, forcing climbers to trust memory, and [[Absolute Certainty]] over sight. There are some regions with [[Forsaken Flower]]s that paint the scene with wounded red amongst the snow.
- Fracture Seams: The lower zones below the Boreal Reach where [[Consonance]] and [[Dissonance]] clash, silver mist rising. Here, the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]]' famous [[Coherence]] gradient is most violent featuring the most of the famous "Magic Dead Zones" where spells fail on the border of many [[Dissonance]] Spikes where spells backfire catastrophically. The ground itself is unstable; the seams shift with the iconic mirrored pools of fractals.
- [[Lunar Abyss]]: Impossible chasm, no sounded bottom, the place where warm mist is rising. Filled with mirrored fractal pools, and past a certain point in depth "up" and "down" become indistinguishable. Paradoxically, it is the zone of the highest [[Vibrational Density]] of the entire [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] when its inner layers align, even more than the summit of the [[Sky Glass]] ascent. The mirrored pools here are massively large and reflect not the sky above, but a different sky with [[Constellation]]s that do not match the stars visible to the climber. Drinking from one of these pools is said to grant a glimpse of the future, always true, never complete, always terrible. For this reason, the [[Lunar Abyss]] has become a favored site for [[Chorus Pillar]] [[Prophet]]s seeking communion with [[Outer God]]s, though it is impossible to determine what answers from below, and is rarely what they intended to reach. _"Go down enough and you will reach the heavens. They are so above as below, as within, as without." - [[Aurelian]], the [[Mythical Virtuoso]] of [[Resonance]]._

**The [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] experience periodic [[Resonance]] Tides** which are waves of high [[Coherence]] that sweep up from the [[Lunar Abyss]] like the tide coming in, following the [[Moon Phase]]. During a Tide, [[Spellweaving]] is amplified; [[Atonalis]] tend to hide and during the Ebb, Magic Dead Zones expand, and demons hunt. A "King Tide" occurs every [[Cycle]], coinciding with the [[Phase of Zenith]], and this is considered both the optimal time for pilgrimage and also the most dangerous.

On the [[Sky Glass]] Ascent, [[Legend]]s speak of a **Phantom Summit**, a peak visible only in peripheral vision, vanishing when directly observed. Those who have reached it return with no memory of the ascent of this last phantom summit, only a profound sense of peace and a single new insight about their [[Motif Awakening]] Wish, and a fragment of [[Sky Glass]] in their pocket that was not there before. Whether this final part is real, a collective hallucination, or the mountain dreaming of itself, no one knows. However, the [[Sonata]] of the Pale [[Moon]] proves this place exists and it is actually necessary to establish one of the [[World-Bending Relics]] in the Phantom Summit to peer the veil of the [[Parlor of the Moon]] and allow for the reunion of [[Selenea]] and the [[Auric Aria]].

Theologically, they are very similar to the Mirrored Waterfalls of the [[Parlor of the Moon]]. It was the place that the [[Auric Aria]] wove for [[Selenea]] as a physical anchor in [[Arcanoria]] which explains the abundance of [[Lunehymn]].

After [[Lacrimosa]] and the [[Law of Relics]] they are a prime place for gathering [[Luceatfilum]] given the amount of seams and transitions they have.

Despite the mountain being filled with [[Sky Glass]] it is commonly referred to as "false [[Sky Glass]]" because of two reasons:

- The [[Sky Glass]] of the mountain loses most of its properties the moment it is severed from the mountain, it's almost as if the [[Sky Glass]] is part of the living system of the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]], severing its connection makes it degrade into dust.
- Real [[Sky Glass]] has the property of being flexible which makes it impossible to get cut with it. The [[Sky Glass]] on the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] however is mostly jagged and doesn't have the tactile properties that real [[Sky Glass]] does. Only certain sections of the higher regions have real [[Sky Glass]], and the way to recognize it is through [[Resonance]].

### The Idyllic and Fatal Paradise

_"Pilgrims climb the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] for many reasons: to test the truth of their [[Motif Awakening]] seeking direction, to a glimpse of their own future in the [[Lunar Abyss]]' pools, to prove their [[Mastery Over Chaos]] — or simply to discover whether they are strong enough to survive a place that does not care whether they live or die. Most of them find the latter in suicidal missions." - [[The White-Touched Archivist]]_

From a distance, the range seems almost gentle, softened by perpetual crescent-shaped veils of mist curling around each summit like sleeping breath, aurora-flickers of residual [[Coherence]] painting the night sky above glacial terraces where frost-shrouded flowers bloom only in twilight. The air tastes of iron and ancient magic. That gentleness is a lie mesmerized by the breathtaking beauty of the inner chambers that pool near the ledges of each waterfall. However, the most crucial detail is how jagged it also is in [[Coherence]]. There are zones of massive [[Coherence]] at the same time there are regions of [[Dissonance]] regarded as "Magic Dead Zones." The intense clash between the [[Lunehymn]] in the [[Leylines]] at the edges of these seams between [[Consonance]] and [[Dissonance]] causes a rise of mist of silver dust that gives the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] its iconic name.

Beneath the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]], invisible until the edge is already underfoot, lies the [[Lunar Abyss]]: an impossible chasm splitting the mountain's heart at the lowest point of the crescent's inner bowl. No bottom has ever been sounded. Its walls are smooth in places, unnervingly so, as though something vast once passed through them, serrated in others as stacked overhangs folding into one another until all sense of scale dissolves and the eye finds nothing to hold.

The waterfalls threading through [[Sky Glass]] do not stop at the chasm's edge. They pour into it, vanishing into a darkness that only becomes visible through the concentrated [[Lunehymn]] that begins creating ripples of light that create a reflection of the cosmos in the same pattern as the Burning Ship Fractal. This gives the iconic name of [[Lunar Abyss]] to the lower levels. These pools are the result of the warm mist that rises from below, warm enough to melt snow on contact, creating strange microclimates where ice and vapor spiral together in forms that mirror the [[Auric Geometry]] of the peaks above, as though the [[Lunar Abyss]] and the summit are the same structure inverted, each dreaming of the other.

The sound of running water, however, persists beneath the ice everywhere on the mountain: promising, treacherous, eternal. The direct connection of [[Lunehymn]] in large quantities is why they are usually regarded as a [[Sacred Site]] for any prophets of the [[Chorus Pillar]]. While the climb is a pilgrimage that creates [[Religion]], these peaks care little for [[Humanity]]. They simply persist, jagged, luminous, indifferent, in the sublime and the lethal share the exact same ground, every waterfall a fracture, every idyllic basin a lid over the [[Lunar Abyss]] below, offering the only gift they have ever given anything that dared to climb them: **the friction that creates [[Ballad]]s.**

### An Expedition Through the Impossible

The [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] have always been a location of significant theological and cultural significance. However, in [[Ages]] II they become the cradle and catalyst of the relationship between the [[Mythical Virtuoso]]. The popular [[Legend]] of the [[Ballad]] is very different from the reality of the timeline of pure chaos which began during the transition between the [[Act of Fate]] 3 and 4 of [[Ages]] II before [[Amadea]] founded [[Iridia]].

The setup and timeline of the [[Events]] for this massive pivotal moment for the [[Mythical Virtuoso]] is the following:

### The Prelude

This is the first major moment of convergence for the [[Mythical Virtuoso]] of [[Ages]] II, although they arrive as strangers, without any [[Legend Title]]s properly yet, and for entirely different reasons:

- [[Luminaire]] and [[Sephira]] arrive at the border of the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] Reach by the Eastern Ridge. [[Luminaire]] is tasked on orders of [[Hollowmarch]] to secure an [[Emberwhisper]] relic found in a [[Secluded Refuge]] between the jagged paths of the Boreal Reach and the Silver Cascades while gathering Purified [[Sky Glass]] from the inner layers of the Whispering Gallery. [[Sephira]] is a bounty hunter that was tasked to escort [[Luminaire]] in her mission, she was sent because she had gained fame during a tavern brawl where she acquired the title of the cornered fire rat.
- [[Orphael]] arrives alone from the South to the Boreal Reach following the [[Legend]] of the [[Lunehymn]] [[Strand Pool]] spring and a deep desire to test himself to stop feeling the crushing shame of his [[Lustful]] nature colliding with his [[Empathetic]] [[Legend Trait]]. He knew the risks and from [[Ballad]]s heard that the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] offer in the Whispering Gallery clarity about oneself, he was on a suicidal mission to understand in his do or die for personal growth as pilgrimage.
- [[Amadea]] is tracking from the shadows [[Orphael]] for information she needs for her own long game about the Violet Grove and his personal ties on connection to one of the powerful nobles of [[Cordelia]]'s family.
- [[Cordelia]] is following [[Amadea]] because they had met earlier during one of [[Amadea]]'s plays, [[Amadea]] brusquely told her to go away. [[Cordelia]] decided they are friends anyway and simply never left.

The context of the scene about meeting depends on these two:

- [[Cordelia]] is the first to meet [[Amadea]] during one of her plays as she's escaping from her own personal tragedy but finds deep solace in the play of [[Amadea]] and [[Artus]], initially following her after she's made it through the [[Age of Embers]] wastes, [[Amadea]] quickly turns down the offer of [[Cordelia]] to partner up given that she's aristocracy but she follows her anyways, and in one clearing where [[Amadea]] gets hurt fighting [[Atonalis]], [[Cordelia]] is there to heal her, surprised [[Amadea]] reluctantly accepts being with her for a while. However, [[Cordelia]] sees in her someone who needs healing while being simultaneously the friend she desperately needs to begin loving again after her betrayal. [[Cordelia]] pretty quickly declares [[Amadea]] her new best friend.
- [[Amadea]] found herself on a third confrontation with [[Luminaire]] before the peaks, but this time [[Amadea]] is caught stealing, she is called a criminal, and [[Cordelia]] uses the last tethers of her political connections to save her, while this mirrors the behavior of [[Artus]] for [[Amadea]] it quickly signals to her that being with [[Cordelia]] will bring nothing good to her, so this is the moment she decides to part ways and to follow [[Orphael]] into the peaks saying that _"Nothing good will come to you if you keep following after me, have you forgotten about the play? What happens to the knight that kept sacrificing himself for her. He dies, and if you keep following me, you will die too. Save yourself, and stop following me."_ [[Cordelia]] is stunted but given what she had done for her already in the [[Resonance]] pugilist fight for her she refuses to press on and follows forward [[Amadea]] through the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]], her ability to deduct where she is, is the very beginning of [[Detective Magic]].

### The Timeline of [[Events]]

The timeline of the [[Crescent Mist Peaks]] is chaotic and it changes between dates and each of the main characters perspectives, alternating between [[Amadea]], [[Cordelia]] and [[Sephira]]. They are tracked per [[Seventh]] and consist of an entire [[Phase]].

-

entries.summary: [[Crystal]] is the element of crystalized reality, of [[Consciousness]] given form in the physical world as an ordered structure, it is the element bound to [[Absolute Certainty]] in [[The Principles of Magic]].
entries.body:
[[Crystal]] is the element of crystalized reality, of [[Consciousness]] given form in the physical world as an ordered structure, it is the element bound to [[Absolute Certainty]] in [[The Principles of Magic]]. [[Crystal]] structures are repeating patterns of fractals that can be enhanced with properties of complex [[Spellweaving]]. This is the core for giving shape to thoughts as as an unbreakable will.

The strength of these structures depends on the ability of the [[Spellweaver]] to imagine them as durable and the mental conviction of it holding true. Despite crystals being commonly rigid structures, they can attain flexible properties akin to nanomaterials and highly complex polymers through the combination of other elemental properties such as [[Flux]] and [[Void]].
